title: delta-compressed-prefix-projection-and-tenant-aware-kv-trimming
creator: Avery Kim
description: Goal: Reduce GPU resident KV footprint and increase cross-request prefix reuse by storing compact delta representations of common prompt prefixes and by trimming tenant-specific tails. We propose a two-part approach: (1) a delta-compressed prefix projection format where repeated prefix tokens are represented as a reference to a canonical base plus a short delta (token diffs or suffix IDs), and (2) a tenant-aware trimming pass that strips low-utility trailing tokens from cached entries based on recent access patterns. The combination aims to: (a) reduce per-tenant GPU KV memory by 25-45% on sampled workloads, (b) improve cache hit rate for cold-start requests via compact replayable segments, and (c) keep tail latency regression under 2% for single-request paths.
technical_design: Implementation notes: introduce a canonical-prefix registry keyed by a 128-bit stable fingerprint (murmur3+salt) and store one GPU-resident canonical slab per fingerprint. Cached entries reference the canonical slab and include a small delta blob (run-length token diffs or pointer to a short suffix slab) that is typically <64 bytes. On read, the runtime reconstructs the KV context by concatenating canonical slab + delta using a GPU memcpy-friendly path. For eviction, maintain a per-shard LRU augmented with a reuse score calculated from recent inter-request intervals and batch coalescing potential. Trimming: periodically analyze tenant access histograms to drop trailing tokens with low attention contribution score (computed offline on a sample of eval prompts) and update the cached delta to its trimmed form. Fall back to full expansion when reconstruction fails (fingerprint mismatch or format version skew).
tradeoffs_and_risks: Tradeoffs: more CPU work on write (compression and fingerprinting) and slightly more GPU memcpy on read for reconstruction. Risk of correctness regressions if deltas are applied out-of-order; mitigated by including a small version and sequence number in delta metadata. Security: fingerprint salts are tenant-scoped and stored encrypted. Operational complexity: adds a canonical registry that must be sharded and consistent across runtime workers; plan to leverage existing shard lease mechanism. Performance risk: worst-case read latency could increase for long-delta chains; limit chain depth to 1-2 and reify longer contexts as new canonical slabs.
plan: Milestones: (1) prototype server-side storage and canonical registry (2 weeks), (2) GPU reconstruction kernel and microbenchmark (2 weeks), (3) integration with batching path + trimming analyzer (2 weeks), (4) canary rollout on dedicated cluster (1 week), (5) broad rollout and monitoring (ongoing). Metrics: GPU KV resident bytes, per-request median and p99 latency, steady-state cache hit ratio, number of delta reconstructions per second, and downstream quality regression measured by evaluation prompt set.
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end correctness for a curated prompt suite. 2) GPU resident KV bytes reduced by >=20% on the canary cluster without >2% latency regression. 3) No quality regressions on regression eval suite (difference <0.5% failure rate). 4) Monitoring alerts and automated rollback on cache-corruption signal.

Initial microbenchmarks (stage): 28% reduction in GPU bytes on a sampled multi-tenant trace, median reconstruction cost 0.4ms per request on A100 (single-threaded memcpy path). Github prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4321
